body.statement: If one role is fixed in advance, or if \(|d|\to\infty\) so that one role is selected with probability tending to one, the selected limit and its symmetric-Wald coverage reduce to the fixed-role normal and nominal-coverage result; the gap-split estimator reduces as a construction to fixed-role late-block proximal inference, with its declared sample-splitting variance rather than the full-pre-period efficiency bound.
body.justification: The reduction verifies compatibility with the published predetermined-role theory and makes the efficiency cost of splitting explicit.
body.gap: The reduction is a required sanity check rather than a novelty claim.
body.consumer: It lets applied users interpret the correction as ordinary fixed-role proximal inference away from the selection boundary.
body.proof_tex:
If role \(s\) is fixed before observing the panel, \(\texttt{lem:fixed-role-linearization}\) and the Gaussian-limit premise used by \(\texttt{thm:selected-gaussian-limit}\) give
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_s-\tau)\Rightarrow A_s+\sqrt rR_s,
 \qquad
 \frac{\widehat\tau_s-\tau}
      {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_s^{\mathrm{conv}}}
 \Rightarrow T_s\sim N(0,1).
\]
Consequently its symmetric Wald coverage converges to \(2\Phi(z)-1\).  The same reduction occurs under diverging loss separation.  Indeed, the ridge expansion in \(\texttt{thm:selected-gaussian-limit}\) shows that
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat L_1-\widehat L_2)
 =\sqrt n(L_1-L_2)+D_n+o_{P_n}(1),
 \qquad D_n=O_{P_n}(1).
\]
If \(\sqrt n(L_1-L_2)\to+\infty\), then \(\Pr(\widehat J=2)\to1\); if it tends to \(-\infty\), then \(\Pr(\widehat J=1)\to1\).  Substitution into the selected expansion therefore gives the corresponding fixed-role normal and nominal-coverage limit.

For the separated construction, fixing the role, or having the early selector choose it with probability tending to one, removes only the random label from \(\texttt{def:gap-split-estimator}\).  The remaining operations are exactly: estimate that role's bridge on \(\mathcal B_n\), average its residual on \(\mathcal C_n\), and estimate the two long-run variances on those same blocks.  Since
\[
 |\mathcal B_n|
 =n-\lfloor\varrho n\rfloor-\lceil(\log n)^2\rceil
 =(1-\varrho)n+o(n),
\]
the fixed-role linearization on these retained blocks has, under \(\sqrt n\)-normalization, variance
\[
 V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}
 =\frac{\Omega_{\psi,s}}{1-\varrho}+r\Omega_{v,s},
\]
rather than the full-pre-period variance \(V_s=\Omega_{\psi,s}+r\Omega_{v,s}\).  In fact,
\[
 V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}-V_s
 =\frac{\varrho}{1-\varrho}\Omega_{\psi,s}\geq0,
\]
with equality only when the pre-bridge influence has zero long-run variance.  Thus the construction reduces to ordinary fixed-role late-block proximal inference with its declared split-sample variance; it does not assert recovery of the full-pre-period efficiency bound.
